references.text: God promises Abraham that he will become the father of many nations, an expansion of the promise to become a great people.
Abraham shall become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him.
God renews His promise to Abraham to make his descendants as numerous as the stars and the sand, and to bless all the nations of the earth through his offspring.
God renews His promise to Isaac regarding numerous descendants and blessing for all the nations of the earth, continuing the covenant made with Abraham.
God renews His promise to Jacob concerning numerous descendants and blessing for all the families of the earth, as a continuation of the Abrahamic covenant.
God promises Jacob that He will make him into a great nation in Egypt, fulfilling the promise to become a great people.
Israel acknowledges that they became a great, mighty, and numerous people, fulfilling God's promise to Abraham.
Paul explains that Scripture foresaw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, preaching the gospel beforehand to Abraham: 'In you all nations shall be blessed.'
Direct fulfillment and elaboration of the promise of a great nation and kings coming from Abraham's offspring.
Direct fulfillment of the promise of a 'great name' from Abraham to David.
Identical to 2 Sam 7:9; confirms the fulfillment of Abraham's promise of a great name in David's line.
Direct elaboration of Abraham's covenant; specifies 'a great people' as 'nations and kings.'
Confirms the unshakable nature of the promise even in the context of judgment; identical wording regarding making them into a great nation.
Messianic expansion of the promise of a great name; from Abraham to the eternal King.
Direct transfer of Abraham's promise to Jacob; confirms that the blessing and dominion are continued.
Direct quote/allusion to Abraham's promise in the New Testament; confirms the eternal validity of the promise.
Direct resumption and expansion of the promise; confirms numerous descendants and victory over enemies.
